A honeycomb of K hexagons covers Manhattan (only hexagons that touch the island are kept), and its corners are the agents. An active corner looks at the three hexagons around it and is pulled toward the fuller ones and away from the emptier ones: it moves a fixed step η along Σ (nᵢ − n̄) uᵢ, where uᵢ points toward the centre of hexagon i. A move is shortened or refused if a hexagon would fold or shrink below the area floor. In live mode the pickups of a 15-minute window keep changing while the same rule keeps running.

items.text:
Stopped, Udi. No 100-cell simulation or geometry changes had started; I had only inspected existing files. The 38-cell result is preserved.

**38 came from the earlier k-means-with-merging baseline**, which produced 38 groups. The original simulator’s comparison mode explicitly sets the hexagon count to match the number of merged groups unless overridden.

So 38 was chosen for that comparison—not because we established it as optimal or mathematically necessary.
